All 9 tests now pass. There were three separate bugs, one in each module:

- **`slug.py`**: Accented characters are now converted to plain ASCII before slugifying, so "Café" becomes "cafe". Runs of non-alphanumeric characters now collapse into a single hyphen. Before, each character became its own hyphen, and accents were dropped.
- **`words.py`**: Words are lowercased before counting, so "The", "the" and "THE" count as one word.
- **`wrap.py`**: `_break_line` indexed past the end of the word list when the last words fit on one line. I added an `i < len(words)` bounds check.

I ran the tests with `uv run --project ../.. pytest ../../tests` because my shell was in `src/textkit`. From the repo root, `uv run pytest` is the same thing.

All 9 tests now pass under `uv run pytest`. There were three bugs:

- **`wrap.py`:** `_break_line` indexed past the end of the word list when the last words fit on one line. It now checks `i < len(words)` first.
- **`words.py`:** `word_counts` counted "The", "the" and "THE" separately. It now lowercases the text before counting.
- **`slug.py`:** every non-alphanumeric character became its own `-`, so runs of punctuation or spaces gave `----`. Accented letters were also dropped instead of being transliterated. It now normalizes to ASCII (`é` becomes `e`) and collapses each run of other characters into a single `-`.

All 9 tests now pass. I made three fixes in `src/textkit`:

- **`slug.py`:** `slugify` now turns runs of non-alphanumeric characters into a single `-`. It also strips accents first, so `Café` becomes `cafe` rather than `caf-`.
- **`words.py`:** `word_counts` lowercases the text before counting, so `The`, `the` and `THE` count as one word.
- **`wrap.py`:** `_break_line` checks `i < len(words)` before reading `words[i]`. That removes the `IndexError` on the last line.

- **`words.py`**: Text is lowercased before counting, so "The", "the" and "THE" are counted together.
- **`wrap.py`**: `_break_line` now checks `i < len(words)` before indexing. Before, it raised `IndexError` once it ran out of words.

- **`slug.py`**: Accented characters were turned into hyphens, and runs of punctuation produced repeated hyphens. It now normalizes to ASCII first (so `é` becomes `e`), and the regex collapses each run of non-alphanumeric characters into a single `-`.
- **`words.py`**: Counting was case-sensitive, so "The" and "the" were counted separately. It now lowercases the text before matching.
